title:
DOXA Studio
Brand Identity & Art Direction
description:
DOXA is a film and creative studio whose manifesto positions internet culture as the ground for a new generation of filmmakers. Drawing on the idea of carnival, it sees memes, digital folklore, and collective participation as material for ambitious storytelling. Its name brings together common belief and divine glory, expressing a desire to connect popular culture with artistic excellence and spiritual purpose.

I developed a visual identity that translates this ambition into a recognizable studio brand. The work spans the logo and its variations, typography, a CRT inspired color system, and applications for YouTube thumbnails and channel branding. Classical references and the texture of screen media give DOXA a visual language that connects its cinematic aspirations with the digital culture it comes from.
concept:
The identity brings classical form into the visual world of the screen. The logo takes its starting point from the classical Greek column, translating the rhythm of its fluting and architectural proportions into repeated contours within the letterforms. These lines give the mark a sense of structure while creating room for the color separation of its CRT treatment.

Berlina balances a clean, contemporary linear structure with the subtle thick-to-thin variation of a pen stroke. Its flowing strokes retain some of the character associated with serif typography, with restrained terminals that keep the overall impression modern. Paired with Nature for supporting text, it connects the expressive logo to a clear typographic system.

The palette draws from the separation of red, green, and blue in CRT screens. Red and blue inform the dominant purple hue, while the highlight carries a 2% green tint in place of pure white. Muted purple tones and this faint green cast bring the screen reference into the broader identity. Together, the column, typography, and color system express DOXA's ambition to elevate the everyday folklore of the internet into lasting cinematic work.
